action-sheet.purpose: Present contextual mobile actions with hierarchy, destructive treatment, cancel, and recovery without forcing a full page transition.
useWhen: A mobile task needs a short list of contextual actions.
Actions need hierarchy, destructive separation, or a cancel path.
The surface should stay tied to the current object or row.
doNotUseWithoutReview: The action list is long, searchable, or needs multi-step input.
Actions are global rather than contextual.
Destructive or permissioned actions lack confirmation policy.
foundations: Defines sheet edge, safe area, action spacing, and touch density.
Owns action labels, destructive copy, cancel, and object context.
Controls action priority, destructive tone, disabled state, and focus.
Sheet overlays mobile content and keeps origin context visible when possible.
Uses sheet entrance/exit motion and reduced-motion fallback.
Requires labelled sheet, touch targets, Escape/back close, and focus containment.
variants: Short contextual list with primary and secondary actions.
Separated danger action with confirmation policy.
Explains unavailable action without hiding it.
motion: Opens from bottom after user action; reduced motion removes decorative slide.
Selected action closes or reports progress according to policy.
accessibility: Actions use full labels and reachable touch targets.
Destructive action is text-backed and not color-only.
Focus and screen reader context remain in the sheet while open.
tests: Trigger opens sheet after user action.
Cancel closes with no side effect.
Destructive action is separated and confirmed when required.
Mobile viewport keeps actions reachable without overlap.

canDecide: Use Action Sheet for short contextual mobile action lists.
Choose action order when product priority is clear.
Separate destructive actions when risk exists.
mustAsk: Action ownership, destructive policy, disabled reason, or mobile back behavior is unclear.
Actions affect money, access, compliance, identity, or irreversible state.
rejectIf: The sheet contains a long form or searchable list.
Destructive action is visually hidden or color-only.
miel.handoff: Confirm trigger object, action priority, destructive policy, cancel/back behavior, and feedback.
